heading: Financial Calculators and Reference Tools
intro: Fin Loom's calculators turn the formulas behind our articles into tools you can test with your own numbers. Each one runs in your browser, shows its formula and assumptions, and explains the result in plain language.
They are educational estimates, not predictions or advice.

tools.title: Inflation Calculator
tools.text: Compare a dollar amount across years using official BLS CPI-U data from 1913 to 2026.

tools.title: Credit Card Debt Payoff Calculator
tools.text: See how long a card balance could take to clear and how much an extra payment could save.

tools.title: Mortgage Payoff Calculator
tools.text: Estimate how much sooner extra payments could pay off a mortgage and the interest they could save.

tools.title: Daily Compound Interest Calculator

tools.title: APY Calculator

tools.title: Savings Interest Calculator

tools.title: Emergency Fund Calculator

tools.title: Credit Utilization Calculator

how: Every calculator follows the same pattern. Inputs sit on the left, the main answer and key figures on the right, and a chart, a detailed table, the assumptions, and a disclaimer follow below. Results update as you type or drag a slider, and an invalid entry is flagged next to the field without clearing the last valid result.
The calculators use fixed assumptions to keep the math transparent. Real returns, rates, prices, and taxes vary, so treat each result as a starting point for understanding, not a forecast.

Want a quick answer before you calculate? The FAQ hubs cover [money and banking](/money-banking/faqs/), [investing](/investing/faqs/), [markets and stocks](/markets-stocks/faqs/), [fintech](/fintech/faqs/), [payments](/payments/faqs/), and [crypto](/crypto/faqs/) in plain language.
